headline: Offshore ramp and asset sale swing Genesis Energy to profit
summary_short: Genesis Energy's Q2 2026 revenue rose 41.0% y/y to $532.0 million as offshore pipeline volumes ramped and it booked a $17.4 million gain on an asset sale, swinging net income attributable to the partnership to $42.9 million from a $0.4 million loss a year ago.
summary_long: Segment Margin rose 25% y/y to $169.5 million, led by a 32% jump in offshore pipeline transportation as the Shenandoah and Salamanca floating production units ramped, plus a $17.4 million gain on divesting non-core pipeline and platform assets. Onshore transportation and marketing segment margin grew 53% on higher crude volumes and stronger sulfur (NaHS) pricing; marine transportation fell 14% on planned dry-dockings. Higher depreciation, interest expense and G&A partially offset the gains. Net income attributable to Genesis Energy swung to $42.9 million from a $0.4 million loss a year ago. The board raised the declared common-unit distribution to $0.20/unit from $0.18 in Q1. Cash rose to $39.3 million; long-term debt eased to $3.10 billion. No forward guidance was issued.

drivers.explanation: Increase driven by higher volumes and revenue across the offshore pipeline transportation network, primarily from the ramping Shenandoah and Salamanca FPU production.
Segment Margin gains in offshore pipeline transportation and a $17.4M asset-sale gain were partially offset by higher depreciation and G&A expense.
Higher segment margin, the $17.4M gain on asset sale, and a $6.0M rise in equity earnings from Poseidon more than offset higher net interest expense.
Marine transportation Segment Margin fell 14% on increased planned dry-dockings and softer inland barge day rates, the one soft spot in the quarter.

confidence_notes: MLP structure — 'EPS' is net income (loss) attributable to common unitholders per common unit; basic and diluted are equal because the Class A Convertible Preferred Units were anti-dilutive in both periods. Net income q/q delta (+530.3%) is real (base was a small $6.8M Q1 print) rather than a sign swing, so it is reported numerically per the same-basis rule; y/y and q/q deltas for EPS and net income against negative/near-zero-sign priors are marked 'n/m'. Distribution declared for the 2026 Quarter was $0.20/unit (paid Aug 14, 2026), up from $0.18/unit declared for Q1 2026. All figures from Form 10-Q for the period ended June 30, 2026 (filed 2026-08-06, accession 0001022321-26-000023).
